doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Fifty-second Street and Teagarden joining Louis Armstrong
summary: 52nd Street was swinging; he recalls the Armstrong Town Hall concert and losing his job when Teagarden joined the All-Stars.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. All the clubs, two sides of the street you know, on that side and this side. Gee, Art Tatum was playing there, and I’m trying to think. Well this was about the time too © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

when Jack got together with Louis Armstrong and they had the Louis Armstrong All- Stars. And I’ll never forget the night I went with Jack in a taxicab over to the Town Hall where they did the, it was a Louis Armstrong concert, well he had Bobby Hackett and I think Bob Haggart played on that. And Dick Cary was playing piano, and Sid Catlett, and Peanuts was on that too. That was recorded for RCA Victor. But I’ll never forget, I was sitting up in the balcony looking right down at all the guys you know. And I’m getting goose bumps you know, listening to all that wonderful music. Well from there on I, that’s when Jack and Louis and the All-Stars with Barney Bigard and Big Sid, that’s when that started, and then I lost my job after Jack went with Louie, and of course I didn’t have a job. So I had to sweat out my union card too.
